newsitem.title: USA: Southern sees rising marketing volumes.
newsitem.headline: Southern sees rising marketing volumes.

text.p: The electricity and natural gas marketing venture between Southern Co and Vastar Resources Inc expects to market 8-10 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) of natural gas and one trillion megawatt hours (mwh) of electricity a year by 2002, a Southern executive said Tuesday.

The venture, to be 60 percent owned by Southern and 40 percent by Vastar, marketed a combined 4.0 bcfd of gas and 6.5 million mwh last year, ranking in the Top 10 among marketers nationwide, Southern executives said.

For Southern, an Atlanta-based utility holding company, the venture forms part of a foundation for competing in the U.S. retail electric market if deregulation opens the grid to competition in the years ahead, the executives said.
"This joint venture would be the generating, supply arm for retail, if it emerges," said Marce Fuller, Southern's Energy Marketing LP chief executive officer.

The venture combines Southern's power marketing operation with Vastar's gas marketing arm. Vastar also has dedicated "substantially all" of its 1.0 bcfd gas production base to the venture under a 10-year supply agreement, the executives said at a Houston press conference.
Southern expects the venture to rank among the top five in energy marketers by the turn of the century. It will focus initially on U.S. wholesale and large industrial customers.

Terms of the venture are still being ironed out, but the venture is expected to begin joint gas marketing operations on September 1 and power marketing by January 1, 1998, following regulatory approval, Fuller said.
